opportunities.title: Broken link in MCP Security Best Practices documentation
opportunities.excerpt:
**Describe the bug**

Two links in the `02-Security/mcp-best-practices.md` documentation page currently point to URLs that return a **404 Not Found** error.

The affected links are under the Advanced Security Resources section of the .md file:

1) [Threat Modeling for AI Systems](https://learn.microsoft.com/security/adoption/approach/threats-ai) - AI threat modeling methodology
2) [Privacy Engineering for AI](https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2021/07/13/microsofts-pet-project-privacy-enhancing-technologies-in-action/) - Privacy-preserving AI techniques

**To Reproduce**

1. Navigate to the [[MCP Security Best Practices](https://github.com/microsoft/mcp-for-beginners/blob/main/02-Security/mcp-best-practices.md)](https://github.com/microsoft/mcp-for-beginners/blob/main/02-Security/mcp-best-practices.md) documentation, and look under Advanced Security Resources subsection in Implementation Resources & Standards section
2. Both URLs return a 404 Not Found error.


Both links should redirect to valid, accessible resources relevant to their original references. If the resources have been moved or removed, the links should be updated to their appropriate replacements.

I just checked these two links and a few others. After the update, maintainers might want to check if all other resources linked in the repo are up-to-date.

opportunities.title: Spec: Committed Claude Code hooks for a check marker and secret-shaped commits
opportunities.excerpt:
## For you

**What.** Commit two Claude Code command hooks, and a small wrapper that records a passing check, so a laptop session can refuse to stop until a check has passed, and so a `git commit` or `git push` of secret-shaped text is refused. This is a technical exploration of those scripts and of fixture tests. It does not run Claude Code, it does not call a model, and every secret-shaped string in it is obviously fake.

**Why.** The lab's rule is that an agent saying "done" counts for nothing until a check passes, and today nothing in the session enforces that. [Goal #187](https://github.com/travism26/harness-lab/issues/187). [docs/skill-workflows.md](https://github.com/travism26/harness-lab/blob/ce892e8899a7f70529c9e2327c894eff593fe408/docs/skill-workflows.md) names Claude Code hooks as enforcement rung 5 and says the repo has no root `.claude/` folder yet. That is still true on [`ce892e8899a7f70529c9e2327c894eff593fe408`](https://github.com/travism26/harness-lab/commit/ce892e8899a7f70529c9e2327c894eff593fe408).

**Done looks like.** `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/`, and `.claude/README.md` exist. `uv run pytest tests/factory` passes, including a new file that feeds fixture JSON to the scripts and reads the settings file. The README says the hooks run with the user's permissions, how to turn them off for one session, and that a match is reported by kind and location only.

## Problem Statement

A session can end, and a commit can land, with no check and with a secret-shaped string in the commit. The factory's own Claude Code loads project settings ([factory/claude.py](https://github.com/travism26/harness-lab/blob/ce892e8899a7f70529c9e2327c894eff593fe408/factory/claude.py#L102-L112)), so a Stop hook that always blocks would hold an unattended Factory run open. The hooks reference's Stop schema is public. Whether the owner's installed Claude Code keeps a turn open for that JSON has not been measured, and [Goal #187](https://github.com/travism26/harness-lab/issues/187) says that measurement is [#193](https://github.com/travism26/harness-lab/issues/193).

opportunities.title: feat(security): Process Sandboxing & Resource Confinement for MCP Child Processes (Linux Namespaces / cgroups)
opportunities.excerpt:
### Summary
When connecting external MCP servers or executing untrusted tool processes (e.g., Python runners, shell tools, third-party adapters), child processes must not inherit the host application's environment, memory space, or privileges. Running child processes without isolation poses high security and stability risks (e.g. secret extraction from environment variables, CPU exhaustion, unauthorized filesystem access).

### Technical Scope
1. **Environment & File Descriptor Hygiene**:
   - Strip sensitive environment variables (`JWT_SECRET`, `API_TOKEN`, database credentials) when spawning child processes.
   - Set `close_fds=True` to ensure internal sockets, database handles, and pipes are not leaked to subprocesses.
2. **Resource Confinement**:
   - Enforce hard limits on RAM usage (memory limits) and execution time (deadlock/runaway query prevention) via cgroups or `resource.setrlimit` on POSIX systems.
3. **Filesystem Isolation**:
   - Confine filesystem access strictly to the assigned workspace directory using Linux namespaces, container boundaries, or unprivileged isolation wrappers (e.g., `bubblewrap` / `nsjail` / restricted sub-shells).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Subprocess executor enforces explicit environment variable allowlists.
- [ ] Hard resource limits (memory ceiling, process timeout) terminate runaway child processes.
- [ ] Child processes cannot access secrets, `.env` files, or directories outside the designated workspace.
- [ ] Regression security tests validating containment.

inboundFeedback.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
inboundFeedback.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.
